evidence.note: Builds early and immediately runs the i32.json per-family spec-test rather than deferring verification to the end.

Uses wabt's reference spectest-interp on individual family jsons (i32, block, simd_const, simd_splat) to establish expected per-family behavior before implementing — fine-grained per-family orientation.
After patch+rebuild, re-runs individual family jsons (i32, simd_const, block) and reads the full output (drops the earlier `| tail`) to see specific pass/fail lines, not just the summary.
Runs an aggregate loop across all jsons twice — once after initial patch and again after the call_indirect fix — treating the overall pass count as a monitored regression signal.

Drills into a specific call_indirect failure: reads the exact json line, disassembles the wasm with wasm2wat/wasm-objdump to localize the genuine cause before fixing (steps 75-79 fix and re-run to green).

reasoning: The agent demonstrates the anchor-8 loop clearly: build → run the relevant per-family json → read specific FAIL/line reasons → fix → re-run to green, with periodic aggregate-runner passes (steps 66, 80) to guard against regressions. The call_indirect diagnosis (steps 70-73) drills into an individual failing assertion using disassembly to distinguish a genuine bug — a touch of anchor-10 engineering — but the visible trajectory is short and early (mostly MVP fixing, two edits) and does not surface the deep SIMD semantic edge-case verification (NaN, saturation, lane order) that would push it to 10, so I place it at 8.
